program_name: Materials Science. This is the correct official English name and the naming question in the task notes is RESOLVED in favour of 'Materials Science' (singular 'Science', plural 'Materials'). Three independent official UNITO sources agree: (a) apply.unito.it course 246 is titled 'Materials Science' and its JSON feed returns "name": "Materials Science"; (b) the UNITO degree catalogue entry is '[0208M22] MATERIALS SCIENCE' (www.unito.it/didattica/offerta-formativa/corsi-di-studio/materials-science and unito.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2025/41578); (c) the programme's own microsite is branded 'Master degree in Materials Science' at www.materials-science.unito.it. Italian official name: 'Scienza dei Materiali'. The variant 'Material Sciences' seen on UNITO's international/English portal pages is an inconsistent editorial rendering, not a distinct or official programme title; the closest genuinely-named UNITO item using that wording is a DIFFERENT programme, the PhD in 'Chemical and Material Sciences' (en.unito.it/postdegree/phd/chemical-and-material-sciences). Do not confuse this master with UNITO's separate BACHELOR degree 'Materials Science and Technology' / 'Scienza e Tecnologia dei Materiali' (en.unito.it/ugov/degree/39772, microsite stmateriali.campusnet.unito.it). UNITO internal degree-programme code [0208M22]; apply.unito.it course id 246; UNITO catalogue id 32130 / Cineca catalogue id 41578.
level: master (second-cycle degree / Laurea Magistrale, 'Postgraduate degree course in Materials science'). apply.unito.it lists 'Type: POSTGRADUATE DEGREE, full-time'; the JSON feed returns type 'MA', type_name 'POSTGRADUATE DEGREE', mode 'FT'. Nominal duration 2 years, 120 ECTS. 'For each year of enrollment, students may choose between full-time or part-time status. Tuition fees vary accordingly.' The programme concludes with an individual research project carried out during an internship at an academic or external/industrial research laboratory plus a final thesis.
teaching_language:
Case 1 - fully English-taught, single-university UNITO degree. apply.unito.it lists 'Study language: English' and the JSON feed returns "language": "en"; the programme overview states 'All lectures and examinations for the Master's degree are conducted in English.' The UNITO catalogue entry [0208M22] also lists the language as English and the microsite is published in English. It is NOT an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree and NOT itself a joint/interuniversity degree: it is a standalone UNITO Laurea Magistrale run by the Department of Chemistry. No Italian-language requirement is published for admission or graduation.

IMPORTANT NUANCE - MaMaSELF: the same LM-53 degree hosts a distinct international track, MaMaSELF / MaMaSELF+ ('Erasmus Mundus Master in Materials Science Exploring Large Scale Facilities'), for which the microsite carries its own course list (www.materials-science.unito.it/do/corsi.pl/BrowseYears?cds=MaMaself) and its own call page (www.materials-science.unito.it/do/home.pl/View?doc=/mamaself/Call.html), and UNITO publishes separate news announcements (en.unito.it/news/erasmus-mundus-master-materials-science-exploring-large-scale-facilities-application-open). MaMaSELF is a two-year consortium programme, also fully in English, in which students study at two of the partner universities and receive a DOUBLE Master's degree; admission to MaMaSELF runs through the Erasmus Mundus consortium's own call, NOT through the apply.unito.it course-246 route described in the rest of this record. Everything else in this record describes the ordinary (non-MaMaSELF) UNITO route. [uncertain - the exact current status of the MaMaSELF track for the 2026/27 intake, and whether MaMaSELF students are formally enrolled under this same [0208M22] degree code, could not be confirmed on a directly-opened official page because the microsite host is unreachable from this environment]

admission_type:
OPEN ACCESS (Italian 'accesso libero' / 'free access' - no numerus clausus, no ranking, no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT) BUT WITH A COMPULSORY QUALIFYING ASSESSMENT that must be passed before enrolment can be completed. The microsite states plainly: 'The Master's degree in Material Science is a free access course' and 'The Master's Degree in materials science is a free-access degree, but in order to enrol, you have to fulfil specific curricular requirements and have an adequate personal background.' The UNITO catalogue lists 'Entry requirements: course without restricted number of places'.

THREE DIFFERENT ROUTES, with different assessments:
1. Applicants with a FOREIGN degree (any citizenship) - apply through the Apply@UniTo portal (apply.unito.it, course 246). Their CV is first evaluated; those admitted to the test are then emailed an invitation to sit a WRITTEN ONLINE TEST on the UNITO Moodle platform. apply.unito.it: 'Applicants will be asked to attend an online test on the Moodle platform. Information about the test will be sent via email to the students admitted to the test after an evaluation of the CV.'
2. Applicants from ITALIAN institutions other than UNITO - register on the UNITO portal, then pre-apply on MyUniTo under 'Enrolments > Evaluation test', which automatically books them for an ORAL ADMISSION INTERVIEW.
3. Applicants from the UNIVERSITY OF TURIN itself - MyUniTo 'Evaluation test' registration only ('There will not be any written test, this is a formal procedure to finalize the application'), followed by the same oral interview.

EXEMPTION (routes 2 and 3): 'All students who have obtained a degree mark of 94/110 or higher are exempt from the interview.' However, 'All students, including those exempted from the interview, must register for the assessment test, to allow the commission to evaluate the qualification.' In the 2024/25 version of the page the exemption was worded differently and narrower ('Students from the Bachelor degree in "Scienza e tecnologia dei materiali" obtained at the university of Turin are exempted from the oral interview'), so this rule has been broadened over recent cycles.

TERRITORIAL CAP: the only published cap is territorial, not academic - apply.unito.it: 'This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.' There is no EU sub-quota and no published total intake figure. Roughly half the student intake is reported to come from outside Italy.

entry_exam_or_test:
YES - a qualifying assessment is compulsory, but it differs by applicant route and it is NOT a competitive/ranked entrance exam (the degree has no restricted number of places).

A) FOREIGN-DEGREE APPLICANTS (Apply@UniTo route): a WRITTEN ONLINE TEST on the UNITO MOODLE platform, preceded by a CV screening. apply.unito.it (a.y. 2026/27): 'Applicants will be asked to attend an online test on the Moodle platform. Information about the test will be sent via email to the students admitted to the test after an evaluation of the CV.' The microsite adds: 'After this procedure, the student will receive an official email from UNITO. Here the student will have to take part to written test on a moodle platform. All the students that applied and have been accepted will receive an email with all the information for the registration to the admission test. In the admission test questions based on the Syllabus will be presented. Admission tests are periodically scheduled as communicated on this website. The selection committee will include at least 2 members of the teaching staff.'

TEST TOPICS (published verbatim on apply.unito.it for 2026/27): '- Fundamental knowledge of mathematics; - Fundamental knowledge of physics; - Fundamental knowledge of chemistry; - Fundamental knowledge of earth science; - Active and passive knowledge of scientific English.' The microsite's Welcome and orientation page expands this: the test is taken in English and covers general questions on the chemical bond and electronic structure in molecules and solids, and the major classes of materials and their thermophysical, mechanical, electronic, optical and magnetic properties (polymers, ceramics, semiconductors, metals), plus basic IT tools (word processing, spreadsheets, presentations) and active/passive scientific English; suggested preparation textbooks are listed there.

B) ITALIAN-DEGREE APPLICANTS (MyUniTo route): an ORAL ADMISSION INTERVIEW held online. 'Admission interview: you will be assessed on your academic knowledge, which should at least equal the basic requirements listed here. Admission interviews are periodically scheduled (see the calendar). Applicants can attempt the interview maximum twice a year.' Interviews are typically held online via UNITO Webex. Published interview dates for the 2025/26 cycle were 5 September, 24 September and 30 October 2025; for the 2024/25 cycle they were 9 September, 30 September, 30 October and 12 December 2024, all at 14:30 online. The 2026/27 interview calendar was not readable on a live official page.

C) EXEMPTION: 'All students who have obtained a degree mark of 94/110 or higher are exempt from the interview' - but they must still register for the evaluation test so the commission can evaluate their qualification.

No published numeric pass mark, no TOLC, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT. [uncertain - the 2026/27 test and interview dates could not be confirmed on a directly-opened official page; the 2025/26 dates come from search-engine renderings of the live microsite and the 2024/25 dates from a Wayback snapshot]
academic_requirements:
ENTRY QUALIFICATION: a Bachelor's degree (Laurea Triennale / first-cycle degree) of at least three years, obtained in Italy or abroad. apply.unito.it: 'You must hold a first-cycle degree (i.e. bachelor's degree) gained after at least 3 years of University education.' The microsite: 'Students who want to apply the Master's Degree in Material Science must be in possession of a Bachelor Degree, or an equivalent University degree of the duration of at least 3 years or another title obtained abroad, recognized as suitable.' Applicants who have not yet graduated may apply and must upload a self-certification of the degree listing all exams passed and the exams still missing.

DISCIPLINARY BACKGROUND - the two official sources word this differently:
- Microsite (Admission requirements): applicants 'must be in possession of a Bachelor's Degree, obtained in Italy or abroad, in one of the following subjects: Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics or Materials Engineering.'
- apply.unito.it (a.y. 2026/27): applicants must 'demonstrate an adequate personal knowledge in the following subjects: Materials Science, Chemistry, Industrial Chemistry, Physics, and Applied Physics.'
Treat the union of the two lists as the practical guide; the microsite version is the one that carries the formal Italian degree-class mapping.

FORMAL ITALIAN DEGREE CLASSES ACCEPTED (from the microsite's 'Minimum academic's requirement' box): Chemical Sciences and Technologies - Classe 21 Scienze e Tecnologie Chimiche (D.M. 509/99) / L-27 Scienze e Tecnologie Chimiche (D.M. 270/04); Physical Sciences and Technologies - Classe 25 Scienze e Tecnologie Fisiche (D.M. 509/99) / L-30 Scienze e Tecnologie Fisiche (D.M. 270/04); Materials Engineering - Classe 10 Ingegneria Industriale (D.M. 509/99) / L-9 Ingegneria Industriale (D.M. 270/04).

FOREIGN DEGREES: 'In the case of foreign degree certificates, the degree must be recognized as equivalent to an Italian Bachelor's Degree according to Italian legislation.' 'For the students who obtained a Bachelor's Degree abroad, they will be accepted is the degree is considered similar to one of those listed above. Candidates who possess an academic title obtained abroad must apply through the procedure of the Athenaeum.'

NO PUBLISHED MINIMUM GPA/GRADE THRESHOLD FOR ADMISSION. The only grade figure published anywhere for this programme is 94/110, and it is an EXEMPTION threshold from the oral interview - not a minimum entry bar. This is a notable difference from several other UNITO English-taught masters, which publish a hard 9.3/10 (102/110) floor on apply.unito.it; course 246 does NOT carry that clause.

NO PUBLISHED MINIMUM CFU/ECTS THRESHOLDS by scientific-disciplinary sector (SSD) - unlike some other UNITO masters, this programme publishes no numeric credit table; adequacy of background is judged by the CV screening plus the Moodle test (foreign applicants) or the interview (Italian applicants).

OTHER PREREQUISITES: 'Applicants are also expected to have basic Information Technology (IT) skills (e.g. text elaboration, use of datasheets, etc.)' and English at CEFR B2 (see language_requirements).

QUOTA / PLACES: no overall numerus clausus ('course without restricted number of places'). The only published cap is territorial: apply.unito.it, 'This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.'

STRUCTURE: 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time or part-time by yearly election; Department of Chemistry, School of Sciences of Nature; interdisciplinary training in chemistry and physics of solids, materials production, manufacturing and testing, with emphasis on characterisation and modelling; concludes with an internship-based individual research project and a thesis. [uncertain - the degree-class list and the wording of the eligibility rules were read from a 2024 Wayback snapshot of the microsite (last update 07/06/2024) because the live host is unreachable; the two official subject lists are not identical and are reported side by side above]
language_requirements:
ENGLISH ONLY - no Italian language requirement is published (the degree is fully English-taught). Required level: CEFR B2. The microsite's Admission requirements page: 'The English language knowledge level must be not less than the B2 level in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).'

HOW IT IS VERIFIED - this programme is unusual among UNITO masters in that it publishes NO accepted-certificate list and NO minimum IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge scores. Instead, apply.unito.it states under 'Language requirements: English' simply: 'Your knowledge of the English language will be verified through the online test.' In other words, English proficiency is assessed inside the Moodle admission test itself, one of whose published topics is 'Active and passive knowledge of scientific English'. For Italian-route applicants, English is assessed within the oral interview.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: an external English certificate (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge/PTE/Trinity) does not appear to be a formally mandatory upload for this specific programme, in contrast to e.g. UNITO's Molecular Biotechnology master which publishes a strict certificate list with minimum scores. However, apply.unito.it's general 'Required documentation' page notes that some postgraduate programmes require 'English language certifications' as additional documents, and the International Students Office may request further documentation at the enrolment step - so applicants who hold a B2+ certificate should upload it, and applicants without one should expect the online test to be the sole proof. No exemption rule (native speaker, prior English-medium degree) is published. [uncertain - the absence of a certificate requirement is inferred from the absence of any such clause on the live apply.unito.it course page and on the microsite; it is not stated anywhere as an explicit 'no certificate needed' rule, and the microsite's live 2026/27 wording could not be opened directly]
required_documents:
A) APPLICANTS WITH A FOREIGN DEGREE - via the Apply@UniTo portal (apply.unito.it, course 246):
1. Valid identity document / passport (passport for non-EU citizens).
2. First-cycle (bachelor's) degree certificate obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or an equivalent/higher qualification recognised as equivalent to an Italian Bachelor's Degree under Italian legislation. If not yet awarded, a self-certification of enrolment listing exams passed and exams still to be taken.
3. Official academic transcript of records with exams, credits (CFU/ECTS) and grades.
4. CURRICULUM VITAE - specifically load-bearing for this programme, because admission to the Moodle test is decided on it: 'Information about the test will be sent via email to the students admitted to the test after an evaluation of the CV.'
5. MOTIVATION LETTER in English or Italian - explicitly required on the course page ('Other requirements: A motivation letter must be added to your application'); Apply@UniTo also lists the motivation letter as mandatory for all postgraduate programmes.
6. Optional but recommended: degree programme syllabus (course description) issued by the foreign institution, with a translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish.
7. English language evidence - no certificate list is prescribed for this programme (proficiency is tested in the online Moodle test), but a B2+ certificate should be uploaded if held.
8. Payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the deadline of the call (same amount whether one or two degree programmes are selected).
LANGUAGE OF DOCUMENTS: 'The entry qualification documents are accepted in the following languages: English / French / Italian / Spanish. If the document is issued in a different language from those listed above, you will have to upload both the original document and its certified translation.'
AFTER SUBMISSION: UNITO may request further documents such as a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore), a Statement of Verification, or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability; the International Students Office may request additional documentation again at the enrolment stage. Non-EU applicants residing abroad must also complete Universitaly visa pre-enrolment.

B) APPLICANTS WITH AN ITALIAN BACHELOR DEGREE - via MyUniTo ('Enrolments > Evaluation test'):
1. Registration on the unito.it portal to obtain MyUniTo credentials (UNITO students are already registered).
2. Pre-enrolment on the 'Evaluation test' page, indicating which interview session is chosen - this doubles as the booking for the admission interview.
3. For candidates who do not yet hold the Bachelor's degree: 'a self-certification of the Degree with all the exams and the enrolment to the missing exams'.
4. Course syllabus / evidence of academic background sufficient for the commission to evaluate the qualification - required even from candidates exempt from the interview ('All students, including those exempted from the interview, must register for the assessment test, to allow the commission to evaluate the qualification').
After a positive interview outcome, enrolment is completed on MyUniTo under 'Enrolments > Matriculation' within the administrative deadlines.

C) ALL CANDIDATES: pass the applicable assessment (Moodle written test or oral interview) unless exempt under the 94/110 rule. [uncertain - list B and the exact document wording were read from the 2024/25 versions of the microsite's Admission requirements and How to apply pages (last updates 07/06/2024 and 01/07/2024); the 2026/27 versions could not be opened]

uncertainty_notes:
NAMING QUESTION FROM THE TASK NOTES - RESOLVED. The official English name is 'Materials Science'. It is confirmed by three independent official UNITO sources: apply.unito.it course 246 (page title and JSON "name" field), the UNITO degree catalogue entry '[0208M22] MATERIALS SCIENCE', and the programme's own microsite branding 'Master degree in Materials Science' at www.materials-science.unito.it (whose very domain encodes the name). Italian official name: 'Scienza dei Materiali'. 'Material Sciences' as seen on UNITO's English/international portal is an editorial inconsistency on that portal, not a distinct programme name; UNITO does separately operate a PhD called 'Chemical and Material Sciences', which is the likeliest source of the confusion. Also note the separate UNITO BACHELOR degree 'Materials Science and Technology' (Scienza e Tecnologia dei Materiali), which is a different programme.

ACCESS PROBLEMS DURING RESEARCH (2026-09-01): (1) apply.unito.it refused WebFetch but was fully retrievable with a standard desktop browser user-agent via curl, including the machine-readable JSON feed at /courses/course/246?json=v1 - this is the primary verified source for this record and its content is quoted verbatim above, including the 2026/27 deadline banner and both intake windows. (2) The programme microsite www.materials-science.unito.it (host 130.186.3.24) refused every direct connection over both http and https, and the campusnet alias scienzadeimateriali.campusnet.unito.it timed out identically; its Admission requirements and How to apply pages were recovered from Wayback Machine raw snapshots (20240613212656 and 20240721153553) fetched over plain http, since web.archive.org over https was unreachable from this environment and rate-limited intermittently. (3) The Wayback index holds NO snapshot of admission_requirements.html or how_to_apply.html later than 2024, so the 2025/26 and 2026/27 wording of those pages is available only through search-engine renderings of the live pages. (4) en.unito.it and www.unito.it remain behind a WAF returning HTTP 403, and unito.coursecatalogue.cineca.it returns HTTP 405 to non-browser requests; content from those hosts is reported from search-engine snippets only and is flagged as such. (5) polito.it (Politecnico di Torino) was correctly excluded as out of scope.

CYCLE-CURRENCY CAVEAT: the recovered microsite snapshots carry 2024/25 content (Admission requirements last updated 07/06/2024; How to apply last updated 01/07/2024). The live pages have demonstrably moved on since then in at least two respects: the interview exemption was broadened from 'UNITO Scienza e tecnologia dei materiali graduates' to the general rule 'all students who have obtained a degree mark of 94/110 or higher', and the foreign-applicant route was clarified to a Moodle written test as distinct from the Italian-applicant oral interview. The apply.unito.it course page (updated 2026-06-23) reproduces the current 2026/27 requirements and is the authoritative source where the two conflict.

FIELD-LEVEL UNCERTAINTIES: (a) teaching_language - the MaMaSELF / MaMaSELF+ Erasmus Mundus track is hosted inside the same LM-53 degree with its own course list and its own consortium call, and produces a DOUBLE degree; its current status for 2026/27 and its formal relationship to the [0208M22] code could not be verified on a directly-opened page. Everything else in this record describes the ordinary UNITO route. (b) application_deadline_eu - the domestic MyUniTo 'Evaluation test' window is year-specific (1 July - 4 December 2024 in the 2024/25 cycle; 1 July - 5 December 2025 in the 2025/26 cycle) and the 2026/27 closing date is not confirmed. (c) application_deadline_non_eu - 29 January 2026 is directly verified in the course JSON feed, but the Universitaly visa pre-enrolment deadline (reported as 15 July 2026) was found in a general UNITO admissions context, not on this programme's pages. (d) entry_exam_or_test - the 2026/27 Moodle test dates and oral-interview calendar are not published on any page reachable from this environment; the 2025/26 dates (5 and 24 September, 30 October 2025) come from search-engine renderings and the 2024/25 dates from a Wayback snapshot. No numeric pass mark is published for either the test or the interview. (e) academic_requirements - the microsite and apply.unito.it publish DIFFERENT subject lists ('Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics or Materials Engineering' vs 'Materials Science, Chemistry, Industrial Chemistry, Physics, and Applied Physics'); the formal Italian degree-class mapping (L-27 / L-30 / L-9) comes from the 2024 snapshot only; and there is NO published minimum grade or minimum-CFU threshold - the 94/110 figure is an interview-exemption rule, not an entry bar, and must not be reported as a minimum GPA. (f) language_requirements - this programme publishes no accepted-certificate list and no minimum IELTS/TOEFL scores; English is verified inside the online admission test. The conclusion that a certificate is not formally mandatory is an inference from the absence of any such clause, not an explicit official statement. (g) required_documents - the Italian-route document list and the domestic window come from the 2024/25 page versions. (h) tuition_or_fees_link - the EUR 156-2,800 range is explicitly the a.y. 2025-26 figure carried on apply.unito.it; the 2026-27 bands were not yet published, and the exact microsite fees-page URL slug is unverified. Talents 4 UniTo eligibility follows from the programme being an English-taught open-access master but was not confirmed on a programme-specific official page for this degree. (i) A terminological tension exists between 'free access / course without restricted number of places' and the fact that a qualifying Moodle test or interview is compulsory: this programme should NOT be presented as automatic-entry, since a negative outcome blocks enrolment ('The successfull Enrollment to the Master's Degree depends on a positive results at the interview'). Equally, it is materially less selective than a numerus-clausus programme, and no competitive ranking exists.
